children: Financial stocks outperformed the broader market this week as investors assessed third-quarter earnings across banks, insurers, consumer finance providers, and capital-markets firms.
The Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund
gained 2.35% over the week, while the S&P 500 (
) fell 0.45%. However, the sector continued to lag the broader market
, as XLF has gained 3.33%, compared with an 11.95% advance for the S&P 500.
Earnings Roundup
Top Line (Revenue):
Eight companies beat revenue estimates, while seven fell short, resulting in a ~53.3% beat rate.
Below are some of the key companies that reported earnings this week:
Blackstone
reported EPS of $1.32,
by $0.06, while revenue fell 1% Y/Y to $3.06B, missing by $150M. AUM reached $1.37T, and management expected double-digit base management fee growth in 2027.
American Express

posted non-GAAP EPS of $4.68, beating estimates by $0.19, while revenue rose 8.8% Y/Y to $20.06B, missing by $60M. The company raised its 2026 GAAP EPS guidance to $18.30–$18.60 and plans to cut global headcount by 5% to control costs.
Synchrony Financial

delivered non-GAAP EPS of $2.68 and revenue of $3.82B, beating estimates on both measures; however, revenue remained flat on a Y/Y basis. Purchase volume rose 8% to $49.7B, and full-year EPS guidance tightened to approximately $9.50.
Capital One Financial

reported non-GAAP EPS of $6.69, beating estimates by $1.19, while revenue rose 6.1% Y/Y, beating by $60M. The company generated $1.8B in annualized Discover integration synergies year-to-date and expects Discover card loan growth to turn positive after several more quarters of contraction.
Chubb

posted EPS of $7.66, topping estimates by $0.86, while net premiums earned rose 3.9% Y/Y to $14.92B, exceeding expectations by $1.41B. The company also reported a record core operating income of $2.98B, supported by strong underwriting and investment results.
CME Group

delivered EPS of $3.02, beating estimates by $0.03, while revenue rose 13% Y/Y to a record $1.74B. Adjusted net income increased 12.1% to $1.08B, supported by record trading activity. Management said fourth-quarter trading volume was running 17% above the prior-year period, putting the company on track for another record year.
Nasdaq

delivered EPS of $1.04, topping estimates, while revenue reached $1.48B, above expectations by $20M, giving the exchange operator a double beat. The company raised its 2026 non-GAAP operating expense guidance to $2.55B–$2.58B, reflecting expected acquisition costs and strong revenue performance.
Other financial companies reported results included KeyCorp
, MSCI
, and Northern Trust
, which beat both EPS and revenue estimates.
Fifth Third
and W. R. Berkley
beat EPS estimates but missed on revenue, while Moody’s
and Globe Life
missed both measures. Huntington Bancshares
met EPS estimates but fell short on revenue.
Overall, financials delivered mixed third-quarter results, with stronger EPS performance than revenue. Investors will watch loan growth, capital levels, and 2026 guidance for further direction.
Earnings next week
Several financial companies are scheduled to report earnings next week, including Visa
, Robinhood Markets
, S&P Global
, Mastercard
, and T. Rowe Price
